instrument_name: RIGL 28-12-3 Minimum wages
figure_or_rule_carried: State minimum wage 15.00 USD/h from 2025-01-01; 16.00 USD/h from 2026-01-01; 17.00 USD/h from 2027-01-01 (P.L. 2025 ch. 222 and 223, effective 2025-06-24). No indexation clause; fixed steps only
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section; live host curl 000)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-12-3.1 Wages for minors; 28-12-5 Employees receiving gratuities
figure_or_rule_carried: Minors 14-15: not less than 75% of the 28-12-3 minimum, but the full minimum for all hours in a week over 24 hours. Tipped (restaurants, hotels, other industries except taxicabs): tip credit = minimum less 2.89 USD; cash wage not less than 3.89 USD/h from 2017-01-01 (so the 2026 maximum tip credit = 16.00-3.89 = 12.11). Full-time students under 19 at nonprofit religious/educational/library/community-service employers: not less than 90% of minimum
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copies of official sections)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-12-4.1 Overtime pay; 28-12-4.3 Exemptions
figure_or_rule_carried: 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/week; fluctuating-workweek method barred for delivery drivers and sales merchandisers; retail Sunday/holiday hours paid at 1.5x under 5-23-2 excluded from the weekly overtime count; municipal firefighters 42-h average workweek over 8 weeks. Exemptions: summer camps, police, public employees with comp time, FLSA white-collar on salary >= 200 USD/week, motor carriers, auto/truck/farm-implement sales and service, agriculture, air-carrier voluntary trades. No daily overtime rule
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copies of official sections)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-14-2 regular paydays; 28-14-2.2 Frequency of payment
figure_or_rule_carried: Regular payday; payday within 9 days of the end of the pay period (next business day if the 9th is a holiday); 3 paydays written/posted notice of a payday change. Weekly pay required for private employees except those whose compensation is fixed at a biweekly, semi-monthly, monthly or yearly rate; state/municipal and religious/literary/charitable corporations excluded; DLT director may permit less-than-weekly (not less than twice a month) on petition with surety bond (two regimes: average payroll above or below 200% of minimum wage)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copies of official sections)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-14-10.1 Payment of wages directly to employee account (direct deposit, payroll card)
figure_or_rule_carried: Direct deposit / payroll card only on the employee written or electronic request and with the employer consent; payroll card: at least one free withdrawal of full net wages per pay period (weekly if paid more often than weekly) and free balance inquiry (phone or online); Reg E protections
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-14-4 Payment on separation by employer
figure_or_rule_carried: Any separation (resignation or discharge): unpaid wages due on the next regular payday. After at least 1 year of service, accrued vacation pay (CBA, written or verbal policy/agreement) becomes wages payable in full or prorated on the next regular payday. Liquidation, merger, disposal or move out of state: all wages due within 24 hours; with >=1 year service also holiday pay, vacation and CBA/policy insurance benefits within 24 hours
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-14-3.1 Payroll deductions (remittance timing)
figure_or_rule_carried: Any payroll deduction must be transferred to the payee within 21 days after the last day of the month of deduction (unless the payee permits otherwise in writing); employee civil action; additional 50 USD/day penalty beyond 30 days after intentional failure or written notice
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-14-12 Employment records (version effective until 2026-01-01)
figure_or_rule_carried: Record of hours worked and wages paid each pay period, kept at least 3 years. The chapter index lists a second version [Effective January 1, 2026] at 28-14-12_28-14-12.htm, NOT archived and live host unreachable: the 2026 record/retention rule is unread
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy; superseding version not reachable)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-57 Healthy and Safe Families and Workplaces Act (28-57-3, -4, -5, -6)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with 18+ employees: 1 h paid sick and safe leave per 35 h worked, up to 40 h/year accrual and use (from 2020); FLSA-exempt assumed 40 h/week; carryover required (use capped 40 h/year) or year-end payout plus front-load; up to 90-day use waiting period for new hires; temporary 180 days, seasonal 150 days; no payout at separation; reinstated on rehire within 135 days. Employers under 18: unpaid protected 40 h. Front-load/PTO 40 h policies exempt from accrual tracking, carryover, payout. Pay = same hourly rate and benefits, never below the 28-12-3 minimum. Max minimum increment 4 h/day. Municipal/state employees excluded. Year = employer-determined 12-month period. Statute counts employees in Rhode Island; no in-state hours threshold for partly-in-state employees
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copies of official sections)

instrument_name: RIGL 15-24 Reporting of New Hires (15-24-1, 15-24-2)
figure_or_rule_carried: New hires and rehires reported within 14 days of the effective date of employment or reinstatement to the Department of Administration, Division of Taxation, or its designee, with the information in 15-24-5 (15-24-5 field list NOT read). New employee completes RI W-4 and federal W-4 on or before the effective date of employment
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copies of official sections)

instrument_name: RI OCSS New Hire Reporting page
authority: RI Department of Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
article_or_section: New Hire Reporting (What is it; Common Questions)
figure_or_rule_carried: Report all new hires/rehires within 14 days to the RI State Directory of New Hires; electronic/magnetic reporters: two monthly transmissions not less than 12 nor more than 16 days apart; date of hire = commencement of employment, no later than first day eligible for compensation; employee = person performing labor in RI for whom employer withholds federal or state income tax; paper by mail (PO Box 335, Holbrook MA 02343) or fax 888-430-6907; penalty 20 USD per violation, 500 USD if conspiracy; multistate employers may designate one state
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 2026 copy)

instrument_name: RIGL 9-26-4 Property exempt from attachment (wages)
figure_or_rule_carried: State exemption: entire wages exempt for debtors on public relief (and for 1 year after relief ends); otherwise only 50 USD of wages exempt under state law; wages of the debtor wife and minor children exempt. State floor is LESS protective than CCPA 15 U.S.C. 1673 (75% / 30x federal minimum), so for ordinary creditor garnishment the federal limit governs (US-FED-011); the 1-year post-relief full exemption is state-specific
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-42-3 Definitions (wages, taxable wage base, other-state employment)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI 'wages' exclude remuneration above the 28-43-7 taxable wage base paid in the calendar year by the employer or predecessor; for that purpose 'employment' includes services constituting employment under any employment security law of another state or of the federal government, so wages already paid by the same employer for other-state employment count toward the RI base (answers MULTI-OQ-2 for RI)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-43-7 UI taxable wage base
figure_or_rule_carried: From 2012: UI taxable wage base = 46.5% of the average annual wage in covered employment in the preceding calendar year, computed each September 30, rounded UP to the next even multiple of 200 USD, effective the next tax year; employers with reserve percentage -24.00 or less: base + 1,500 USD. 2026: 30,800 / 32,300 (US-RIP9V-001): 30,800 + 1,500 = 32,300 reconciles
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy); 1,500 step derived arithmetically against US-RIP9V-001

instrument_name: RIGL 28-40-1 TDI employee contributions and taxable wage base
figure_or_rule_carried: TDI taxable wage base = greater of 38,000 USD or (maximum weekly benefit at September 30 x 30 / 0.36), rounded up to the next 100 USD, effective next 1 January; employee rate = fund cost rate (12-month disbursements to Sept 30 / taxable wages 12 months to June 30, x100, rounded down to 0.1%; fund-balance adjustment rule), set by November 15 each year. Employee-only contribution. 2026: base 100,000, rate 1.1% (US-RIP9V-001)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-39-2 TDI definitions (employment = chapter 42 definition)
figure_or_rule_carried: For TDI/TCI 'employment' has the same definition as in chapter 42 (Employment Security), so TDI coverage of a multistate worker follows the UI localization test: TDI is withheld where the worker is localized in RI for UI (answers MULTI-OQ-3 for RI)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RI DLT Employer Tax Unit: Frequently Asked Employer Tax Questions
authority: RI Department of Labor and Training, Employer Tax Unit
article_or_section: Accounts and Control; Status and Registration; Collections
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly Tax and Wage Report TX-17 covers Employment Security (UI), TDI and Job Development Fund in ONE report and ONE payment; due last day of month after quarter (Jan 31, Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31); zero report required; employers and payroll services with 25+ employees must file wage data electronically; ACH credit/debit, no credit card; corrections up to 3 years/12 quarters; late: interest 1.5%/month, 25 USD per report (+25/month, max 200), 10% of tax unpaid; employer that fails to deduct TDI when wages are paid cannot recover it from later pay (28-40-4); employee contributions to 401(k), medical/disability insurance and Section 125 plans excluded from UI and TDI wages; registration by Business Application and Registration (BAR) form (ri.gov/taxation/BAR), liability date = first wages paid in RI; remote RI employee: RI location = employee home address; localization per 28-42-4/5/6; domestic employers subject to UI and TDI at 1,000 USD cash wages in any calendar quarter (28-42-8); PEOs not recognized, each entity reports under its own account, no common paymaster; account closure TX-13; Employer Tax unit moved from Division of Taxation to DLT on 2022-04-11
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 2026 copy; dlt.ri.gov 403 to curl)

instrument_name: RI Division of Taxation Withholding Tax Filing and Transmittal Requirements v.1 12/2025
article_or_section: WTM; RI-941; W-2s; RI W-3; 1099s; portal upload
figure_or_rule_carried: WTM (RI-941M) monthly non-quarter months due 20th of next month (electronic filers pay only); RI-941 quarterly return and reconciliation due last day of month after quarter, used by all withholding employers; e-file/pay mandatory for weekly payers, monthly payers averaging >=200 USD/month, or entities with >=5,000 USD combined annual tax liability or >100,000 USD gross income; bulk filers via Payroll Letter of Intent to Tax.VendorForms@tax.ri.gov; amended returns 24 months on portal. W-2: every employer with RI employees provides W-2 data to RI; electronic mandatory if SSA e-file required AND 25+ RI employees, or any RI tax credit; due January 31; EFW2 format, .txt ASCII only, zip if >5 MB, max 49 MB, upload via Tax Portal; RS State Wage Record required; SSN required. 1099s must be filed even without RI withholding
verification_method: inspected directly (PDF read locally, PyMuPDF text)

instrument_name: 2026 Rhode Island Employer Income Tax Withholding Tables booklet: percentage method and exemption amounts
figure_or_rule_carried: Percentage method, all filing statuses. Annual Table 7: 0-82,050 at 3.75%; 82,050-186,450: 3,076.88 + 4.75%; over 186,450: 8,035.88 + 5.99%. Weekly: 0-1,578 3.75%; 1,578-3,586 59.18+4.75%; over 3,586 154.56+5.99%. Biweekly breakpoints 3,156 / 7,171; semimonthly 3,419 / 7,769; monthly 6,838 / 15,538; quarterly 20,513 / 46,613; semiannual 41,025 / 93,225; daily 315.58 / 717.12. One withholding exemption: weekly 19.23, biweekly 38.46, semimonthly 41.67, monthly 83.33, quarterly 250.00, semiannual 500.00, annual 1,000.00, daily 3.85; exemption amount is ZERO when period wages exceed weekly 5,592.31 / biweekly 11,184.62 / semimonthly 12,116.67 / monthly 24,233.33 / quarterly 72,700 / semiannual 145,400 / annual 290,800. Steps: exemptions x amount subtracted from wages, then table. Worked example (oracle): weekly 2,195.00, 1 exemption: 2,175.77 taxable, 59.18 + 28.39 = 87.57. Supplemental flat rate 5.99% (instruction 12) or aggregate method. RI W-4 mandatory in addition to federal W-4 (since 2020-01-01); allowances capped at 10 on line 1E; EXEMPT / EXEMPT-MS yearly. No rounding rule stated
verification_method: derived arithmetically (booklet worked example reproduced; annual breakpoints / 52 = weekly)

instrument_name: RIGL 6-48-8 Social security number protection
figure_or_rule_carried: No person may make all or part of an SSN available to the public, print it on an access card, require it over an unsecured connection, or print all or part of it on materials MAILED to the individual unless state/federal law requires it (mailed SSN may not be visible on postcard or envelope); internal verification/administrative use and uses required by law allowed; civil fine up to 3,000 USD, knowing violation misdemeanor up to 5,000 USD. No pay-statement-specific SSN truncation rule: a mailed paper pay statement may not carry any part of the SSN (no law requires it on a pay stub)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-41-35 Temporary caregiver benefits (TCI)
figure_or_rule_carried: TCI: bonding (birth, adoption, foster) or caring for a seriously ill child, parent, parent-in-law, grandparent, spouse or domestic partner; 30 days written notice to employer; job restoration and employer must keep existing health benefits during the leave (employee keeps paying its share); TCI + TDI capped at 30 x weekly benefit rate per benefit year. Week cap in this archived copy: 4 (2014), 5 (2022), 6 (2023). CONFLICT: DLT release of 2025-12-18 (US-RIP9V-001) says up to SEVEN weeks, and tier-B leads say EIGHT weeks from 2026-01-01; the archived statute is older than the amendments. The 2026 week cap is NOT settled at tier A (benefit-side only; no payroll rate impact)
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback copy, snapshot predates later amendments)

instrument_name: RIGL 28-42-8 Exemptions from employment (UI and, via 28-39-2(14), TDI)
figure_or_rule_carried: Excluded from UI (and TDI) employment: domestic service in a private home below 1,000 USD cash in every calendar quarter of current or preceding year; family employment (child, spouse; child under 18 of parent sole proprietor/SMLLC or parents-only partnership); other states and federal government; churches, church-controlled religious organisations, ordained ministers and members of religious orders; sheltered workshops, work-relief, hospital patients, inmates; railroad (RRUIA); 501(a) organisations below 50 USD per quarter; casual labour outside trade or business; golf caddies; commission-only real estate and insurance agents; full-time co-op students in credit programs; small-crew fishing boats paid by share; AmeriCorps; self-employed. Agriculture is NOT among the exemptions listed here
verification_method: inspected directly (Wayback 2026 copy of official section)

instrument_name: RI Division of Taxation guidance page H.R. 1 (Public Law 119-21): Rhode Island decoupling
figure_or_rule_carried: Rhode Island decoupled from federal H.R. 1 (enacted 2025-07-04) in its FY2026 budget (H 5076 Sub A as amended, Article 5 sections 3-5; impacted RIGL 44-11-11 and 44-30-12); PIT emergency regulation 280-RICR-20-55-16 effective 2025-12-15. Advisories 2025-18/2025-20 not read: which individual items (e.g. federal tips/overtime deductions, which are below federal AGI) are decoupled is not confirmed here. No change to the 2026 withholding method (booklet US-RIS5-019). Same page: tax changes effective 2026 are non-payroll (hotel 2%, short-term rental 5%, kratom from 2026-04-01, non-owner-occupied property tax from 2026-07-01)
verification_method: quoted from authority page (Wayback 2026 copy)
